overview: Several systems rotate across the West this week. Rain and mountain snow hit the Sierra and Cascades first, then a northern storm train reaches the Rockies and Montana into Tuesday.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Strong winds arrive Sunday morning ahead of a storm. Rain falls in the valleys and snow in the mountains from Sunday midday, with snow levels dropping as low as 6500 feet overnight into Monday. Mammoth leads, with 15" total and its biggest day on Monday. The NWS is calling for more, 12 to 24 inches Sunday night through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Dry weather holds through Saturday, then a wet, unsettled pattern takes over Sunday into mid-week. Heavy precipitation is expected Sunday afternoon into the overnight hours, with gusty southerly winds over the Sierra crest. Kirkwood leads at 14" total, with its biggest day on Monday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A fast system brings a round of snow to the central and southwest passes tonight into Saturday morning, then clears. Weaker Pacific systems follow late Sunday through Tuesday with light mountain snow. Jackson Hole leads at 12" total. The NWS is calling for more, 16 to 30 inches Friday through Tuesday night, and a Winter Storm Warning runs Friday into Saturday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A weak ridge brings a brief break Saturday. Another system arrives Sunday, with rain spreading inland and winds possibly picking up Sunday night. Forecasters are unsure of the storm's track, which could mean much stronger winds. Crystal Mountain leads at 11" total. The NWS is calling for more, 10 to 23 inches Friday through Wednesday night.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a deep Pacific trough could bring renewed precipitation to the Pacific Northwest and West late in the week, around Friday Dec 4, though its models disagree on the timing.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
